plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Libby AGI No. 1 and Libby AGI No. 2, Lea County, New Mexico
ama_definition: By rule the end-of-injection (year 20) plume plus a half-mile buffer combined with the year 25 plume, but because the difference is small the operator set the AMA equal to the MMA (p59).
mma_definition: The modeled stabilized plume (about 651 acres, 50 years after injection stops) plus a half-mile buffer (p59).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None rated above low. Surface equipment (pipeline flanges, valves, wellheads) is described as the most likely failure point during injection; three wells penetrate the injection zone in the MMA, one plugged well inside the stabilized plume (p61-66).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection soil gas sampling near selected well locations in the MMA (scheduled Q4 2025, third-party lab), ambient H2S and CO2 levels set during amine unit commissioning, and initial reservoir pressure measurements; after that, SCADA operational data serve as the baseline (p75-78, p84).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 through e-GGRT (draft in Appendix D); injected volumes and pressures also reported to NMOCD under Class II rules; records kept at least three years; amended plan with an updated plume due before the end of year 5. No commitment to publish measurement data (p84, p86-87).

rows.detail: Volumetric flow meter downstream of the amine unit measures acid gas injected; composition by continuous gas chromatograph or regular lab samples, averaged quarterly. Received is set equal to injected.
rows.location: In-plant, downstream of the amine unit
rows.evidence_quote: The flow rate of the acid gas being injected will be measured with a volumetric flow meter

rows.detail: SCADA/DCS records injection pressure, temperature, rate and gas composition around the clock from a wellhead gauge; pressure kept below the 4,525 psig surface limit; ESD valves with high/low pressure shutoffs.
rows.location: Libby No. 1 and No. 2 wellheads; plant and pipeline
rows.trigger_or_response: Data outside normal range or deviation suggesting a pathway: personnel investigate and shut in the well if needed.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection pressure, temperature, rate, and annular pressure will be monitored continuously.

rows.detail: Pressure gauge on the tubing-casing annulus (filled with corrosion-inhibited diesel), recorded by SCADA.
rows.trigger_or_response: Change in annular pressure is treated as a possible leak and investigated.
rows.evidence_quote: a pressure gauge is placed on the casing annulus.

rows.detail: Annual MITs required by NMOCD rule to confirm each well and wellhead hold operating pressure.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT: well isolated and leak mitigated.
rows.evidence_quote: NMOCD regulations require that an MIT be performed annually to confirm that the well and wellhead can properly hold the appropriate amount of pressure.

rows.detail: Initial reservoir pressure measured before injection as a baseline; no downhole gauges or observation wells described for ongoing monitoring.
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant pressure deviations over time analyzed for leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: Initial reservoir pressure measurements will be taken before commencing injection operations.

rows.detail: Field inspections of detectors, gauges and leak signs such as vapor plumes and ice; daily at the gas plant, as needed at wells.
rows.location: DKL Libby Gas Plant; Libby No. 1 and No. 2 well sites
rows.trigger_or_response: Vapor clouds or ice found: corrective action taken.
rows.evidence_quote: Regular inspections are to be conducted by field personnel at the DKL Libby Gas Plant and the Libby No. 1 and No. 2 wells.

rows.detail: Field personnel wear personal H2S detectors (alarm at 10 ppm) and CO2 alarms (above 0.5%).
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, verify detectors, secure facility and mitigate leak.
rows.evidence_quote: Delek field personnel are required to wear personal H2S detectors that trigger an alarm at 10 ppm

rows.detail: Fixed ambient H2S detectors in the plant and at both well sites, tied to SCADA, used as a proxy for CO2; 10 ppm high alarm, 90 ppm emergency shutdown.
rows.location: In-plant; Libby No. 1 and No. 2 well sites
rows.trigger_or_response: 10 ppm: alarm and response; 90 ppm: emergency shutdown; leak quantified from operating conditions.
rows.evidence_quote: Ambient H2S detectors are located throughout the DKL Libby Gas Plant and near the Libby No. 1 and No. 2 wells with local alarms

rows.detail: Annual soil gas samples near selected well penetrations in the MMA, including the plugged Federal C No. 1 inside the plume, analyzed by a third-party lab; continues through post-injection.
rows.location: Selected artificial penetrations within the MMA (number not stated)
rows.evidence_quote: annual soil gas monitoring samples taken near identified wells within the MMA

rows.detail: Relies on public networks: nearest station NM03 (about 12.2 km away, called a TexNet station in the plan) plus the USGS and NMTSO online catalogs; watches for M2.0+ within 9.08 km. No site seismometers.
rows.trigger_or_response: M2.0+ event within 9.08 km: review injection volumes and pressures for signs of leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: Delek will monitor for any seismic event of 2.0 magnitude or greater that is detected within the 9.08 km radius

rows.detail: Existing 3D seismic used to locate the nearest fault outside the MMA; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: The nearest fault identified from a 3D seismic is located approximately 1.9 miles east-northeast of the Libby No. 1 and No. 2 wells

rows.detail: Baseline ambient H2S and CO2 concentrations to be set during amine unit commissioning; no ongoing ambient CO2 monitoring described beyond personal CO2 alarms.
rows.evidence_quote: Baseline atmospheric H2S & CO2 concentrations are to be established during commissioning of the amine unit.

rows.detail: Corrosion control checked through periodic inspection of surface equipment, analysis of liquids taken from the line, and cathodic protection inspections.
rows.evidence_quote: The internal and external corrosion control programs are be monitored for effectiveness by way of periodic inspection of surface equipment

rows.detail: Tracking of drilling activity and permits in the MMA, coordinating with NMOCD and operators on well design.
rows.evidence_quote: Delek will routinely monitor for drilling activities and permits within the MMA

rows.detail: Leaks calculated from operating conditions (pressure, rate, CO2 fraction, opening size, duration) rather than surveyed, because of H2S; Subpart W used for equipment between meter and wellhead; flare blowdowns reported.
rows.location: Surface equipment between flow meter and wellheads; flare
rows.evidence_quote: Equations from Subpart W – Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems §98.232 are to be used to calculate CO2 emissions from equipment

rows.detail: Plume model to be updated with measured well conditions and the AMA/MMA revised in an amended plan before the end of the first five years of injection.
rows.evidence_quote: an amended MRV plan is to be submitted for this facility with an updated plume extent based on measured conditions in the wells

notes: Pre-construction plan: wells scheduled to be built Q1 2026 and operating Q2 2026 (p3), yet p82 says injection begins Q3 2025. Acid gas is about 80% CO2 / 20% H2S, so H2S detection is the main CO2 proxy and the plan rules out direct leak surveys for safety (p78, p81). Fixed detector set points conflict: Table 6 gives 10 ppm alarm / 90 ppm shutdown (p65), text says 'setpoints at 10 ppm and alarm at 15 ppm' (p75). The seismic section calls NM03 a TexNet station and cites a nonexistent Figure 42 (p77). Soil gas location count is not stated. Atmospheric CO2 coded mentioned_only because only a one-time commissioning baseline is described. Figures and Appendices A-D (plot plan, well table, draft report) are images or not in the text. Printed page numbers are one less than PDF page numbers used here.
